articles.title: How India’s urban housing story has changed: Over 1 crore homes completed, 1 crore more families targeted
articles.summary: Real Estate News: India’s urban housing story has moved beyond simply building homes, with the government’s flagship housing programme now covering everything from self.
articles.body: India’s urban housing story has moved beyond simply building homes, with the government’s flagship housing programme now covering everything from self-construction to affordable housing projects, rental homes and interest support on home loans.Under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) and its second phase, more than 1 crore houses have been completed and delivered, while 1.25 crore houses had been sanctioned as of August 9, 2026, according to government data released by the Press Information Bureau (PIB). PMAY-U 2.0 aims to support another 1 crore families through its four verticals.Beneficiary-Led Construction: Up to Rs 2.5 lakh for EWS families building on own landBeneficiary-Led Construction (BLC) is meant for EWS households that already own land and want to build a house on it. Financial assistance can go up to Rs 2.5 lakh, while the completed dwelling can have a maximum carpet area of 45 sq metres.Of the 18.38 lakh houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0 by August 9, 14.40 lakh were under BLC. Households owning pucca homes of less than 21 sq metres may also be considered for expansion up to 30 sq metres, subject to the scheme conditions.Affordable Housing in Partnership: Subsidy for EWS buyers in project-built homesAffordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) applies to EWS beneficiaries purchasing homes developed as affordable housing projects rather than constructing on their own plots. Public or private agencies can build units with carpet areas between 30 and 45 sq metres, with combined assistance from the Centre and states going up to Rs 2.5 lakh for each eligible unit.About 2.48 lakh homes had been sanctioned under AHP as of August 9. Unlike BLC, which is linked to construction on a beneficiary’s own land, AHP connects government assistance to homes supplied through organised projects.Affordable Rental Housing: Rental homes for migrants and low-income urban workersAffordable Rental Housing (ARH) is meant for EWS and LIG households that require rental accommodation rather than an owned home. Intended beneficiaries include migrants, homeless people, working women, industrial and construction workers and people earning livelihoods in the informal or contractual economy.The housing is also expected to have basic infrastructure such as water supply, sanitation, sewerage or septage systems, internal roads and health facilities. About 13,046 dwelling units had been sanctioned under the rental housing component by August 9.Interest Subsidy Scheme: Home-loan support for EWS, LIG and MIG borrowersThe Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS) works through the housing-finance system and covers eligible home loans taken by EWS, LIG and MIG households. To qualify, the loan must have been sanctioned and disbursed on or after September 1, 2024 and have a tenure of more than five years.The benefit applies to eligible loans for the purchase, repurchase or construction of a house. Around 1.36 lakh houses had been covered through the interest subsidy component by August 9.The housing programme has also increased the role of women in formal property ownership. Of the 1.25 crore homes sanctioned across PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, 1 crore had been allotted either in the name of the female head of the household or in joint ownership, according to PIB.Digital monitoring has become another part of programme delivery, with PMAY-U 2.0 using a common platform connecting applicants, urban local bodies, states, Union Territories and implementing agencies. Construction can be geo-tagged and tracked through five stages, while the first PMAY-U phase remains open until September 2026 for already sanctioned homes and PMAY-U 2.0 continues through 2029.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: St Pauls Carnival seeks community views to protect its future
articles.summary: Organisers of St Pauls Carnival in Bristol are asking the public what they want to see improved.
articles.body:
A chief executive of a city's carnival says he wants to create a "strong baseline" for the annual event so it can be enjoyed for future generations.

A full-scale St Pauls Carnival in Bristol, which usually attracts about 150,000 people, has not taken place since July 2023, although many people attended community workshops and unofficial celebrations this year.

As the event edges closer to its 60th anniversary in 2028, Ricardo Sharry, chief executive of the community interest company (CIC) behind the event, said he wanted cross-generational community input to drive the organisation forward.

A survey is taking place until 3 October asking carnival attendees to suggest how it could be improved.

Board members of the CIC said the procession and street event in July this year would be scaled back to avoid "unnecessary" risks.

Instead, a smaller programme of community events , workshops and family activities were held, while planning for a possible return in 2027 continued.

Looking ahead, Sharry said: "We want to make sure that, in the next 60 years, we're still celebrating carnival" by understanding what the public wants.

Sharry said organisers wanted to hear from young people and elders because it was a "multi-generational event".

"If you've been to carnival or you think about carnival as July approaches, and you've got something to say, then add to it," he said of the survey.

"These contributions will determine how money should be spent for influence training, youth engagement, street parties and licensing.

"Carnival means different things to different people, but we need a good foundation of information that says what the community needs," he added.

St Pauls Carnival CIC is also working on a project called the Carnival 365 programme.

Julie Syer, its operational manager, said it was important for the city to have a presence throughout the year celebrating its cultural heritage and St Pauls community.

Another change the organisation is implementing through its programme is a scheme called Carnival Futures Academy.

The project aims to teach people of all ages what it is like to work behind the scenes within the CIC.

Syer said people would be able to understand what it was like to work in crowd management, health and safety, stewarding and security.

She said it was important to have such a project so people could learn "we are not just the fun police having to apply legislation".

Sharry confirmed there would be carnival activity in 2027 and again in 2028, when Bristol marked 60 years since the first event.

However, he said a full-scale return depended on establishing a sustainable model which could be repeated year on year.

articles.title: Bootle house fire investigations continue
articles.summary: A woman and three children died in the blaze and another casualty was taken to hospital, police say.
articles.body:
Investigations are continuing after a mother and three children died in a house fire on Merseyside.

Another casualty who was outside the property in Stone Square in Bootle, Sefton, when fire crews arrived during the early hours of Tuesday was taken to hospital.

The Bishop of Liverpool the Rt Rev Ruth Worsley and Bishop of Warrington the Rt Rev Simon Robinson said they are "deeply saddened to hear of the devastating incident".

"Our thoughts and prayers are with their families and loved ones at this unimaginably difficult time," they added.

Six fire engines were called out at the height of the blaze at the semi-detached property.

Firefighters searched the house where they discovered four people in an upstairs bedroom who were showing no signs of life, Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service said.

A joint investigation involving Merseyside Police and Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service is expected to continue into this afternoon.

A police van remains at the scene at the cordon of the cul-de-sac.

Dozens of tributes including cards, flowers, candles, teddy bears and pink and blue star-shaped balloons have been laid on the pavement next to the cordon.

Kevin Longshaw, area manager for Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service, described it as a devastating incident, and their thoughts were very much with the family and friends of those who had lost their lives and been injured.

He said they would work closely with relevant colleagues to determine the cause of the fire.

articles.title: Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli back in action: Shubman Gill-led India to assemble in Thiruvananthapuram for West Indies ODIs
articles.summary: Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, and Ravindra Jadeja return as Shubman Gill's India squad gathers in Thiruvananthapuram ahead of the 3-match ODI series vs West Ind...
articles.body:
India's ODI squad under Shubman Gill will gather in Thiruvananthapuram by Thursday ahead of the West Indies series.

Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma return to action, alongside Ravindra Jadeja, making his ODI comeback after a lengthy absence.

Nitish Kumar Reddy was pulled from Asian Games duty to build bowling workload, with Gambhir hinting he could play alongside Hardik Pandya.

IND vs WI ODIs 2026: India squad arrival details, full schedule, and key player updates

India's ODI unit is reportedly set to come together in Thiruvananthapuram by Thursday, September 24, as preparations ramp up for the three-match series against West Indies under Shubman Gill's leadership.

According to The Times of India, a chunk of the squad will land in the city on Wednesday night ahead of the series opener, while the remainder trickle in a day later to complete the group.

This series marks a notable comeback for two of India's biggest names, with both Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma slotting back into the fold. Ravindra Jadeja, too, makes his way back into the 50-over setup, having been left out since the ODI series against New Zealand earlier in the year.

Their return comes at a time when several of India's regular white-ball names, vice-captain Shreyas Iyer, Ishan Kishan, Jasprit Bumrah, and Axar Patel, are all tied up with Asian Games commitments in Japan. That absence has opened the door for the likes of Ruturaj Gaikwad, Auqib Nabi, and even a veteran like Jadeja to get a look-in.

Nitish Kumar Reddy pulled from Asiad to build workload

With Hardik Pandya sidelined through injuries, the selection panel took the call to withdraw Nitish Kumar Reddy from the Asian Games squad as they wanted the young all-rounder to get proper game time and gradually ramp up his bowling load.

There's plenty riding on this series for KL Rahul as well, who'll be looking to reaffirm his standing as India's go-to wicketkeeper-batter in the ODI format. The team management has, at various points, experimented with handing Ishan Kishan the gloves and giving him extended opportunities behind the stumps.

But Rahul's steady returns in this format, paired with the kind of big-match experience that'll matter in South African conditions, keep him firmly in the picture as the preferred option. He's currently putting in the hours at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, fine-tuning his preparation ahead of the series.

With so many first-choice names away in Japan, this West Indies series has quietly turned into a proving ground of sorts. It is a chance for fringe players to stake a claim, for senior stars to shake off the rust, and for the team management to figure out its bowling combinations well before the business end of the season arrives in South Africa.

articles.title: Rats filmed running across tables at Rajkot McDonald's, civic body takes action
articles.summary: RAJKOT: A video showing two rats running across tables and chairs inside a McDonald’s outlet in Rajkot has gone viral on social media, prompting the c.
articles.body: RAJKOT: A video showing two rats running across tables and chairs inside a McDonald’s outlet in Rajkot has gone viral on social media, prompting the civic action.The video, recorded by a customer, shows the rats moving across tables and seating areas used by customers in the outlet.Municipal health officer Jayesh Vakani said the civic authorities verified the video and found that the rats were in the party area of the outlet.“There are two areas at McDonald’s separated by glass partitions. One is the dining area, while the other is used for parties. We verified the video and found that the rats were in the party area, and they may have entered from outside,” Vakani said.He said the inspection did not reveal a hygiene issue at the outlet, but stressed the need for proper pest-control measures. “That is why we collected an administrative charge from them,” Vakani said.McDonald’s charged Rs 3,000As part of the action, the food department collected samples of toned milk and strawberry fruit crush from Hard Castle Restaurant Pvt Ltd, which operates the McDonald’s outlet at Greenland Chowk. The establishment was also charged Rs 3,000.The samples were collected under the Food Safety and Standards Act and sent to a laboratory for analysis.The action against McDonald’s was part of a wider surveillance drive by the Rajkot Municipal Corporation’s food department targeting food adulteration and unhygienic practices.53 food establishments inspectedDuring the drive, civic officials inspected 53 food establishments, including restaurants, hostels and canteens. They destroyed around 65kg of stale and inedible food, issued notices to 18 establishments for violations related to food storage, licences and hygiene, and collected Rs 17,000 in administrative charges.A sample of used palmolein oil was also collected from Restaurant Brands Asia Ltd, which operates Burger King at Crystal Mall on Kalawad Road, and a notice was issued.At Leuva Patel Girls Hostel, officials destroyed 20kg of stale wheat flour, while another 20kg of expired popcorn packets was destroyed at Phenol Institute. Both establishments were issued notices over licensing and storage issues and charged Rs 1,000 each.At Vivanta Girls Hostel, officials destroyed 5kg of rotten potatoes and collected a Rs 1,000 administrative charge.At Prem Caterers, which operates the canteen at Mahila College, around 20kg of stale and inedible food was destroyed and a Rs 3,000 charge was collected.The inspections were carried out across areas including Kalawad Road, Morbi Road, Gondal Road, University Road, Kothariya Road and Nirmala Road, with the food department issuing notices to several establishments over shortcomings related to hygiene, licensing and storage.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Rajkot | Silver Rate in Rajkot | Bank Holidays in Rajkot | Public Holidays in Rajkot | Rajkot AQI | Weather in Rajkot | Petrol Price in Rajkot | Diesel Price in Rajkot | CNG Price in Rajkot | LPG Price in RajkotStay updated with the latest Rajkot news.
